# Linear models {#sec-linear-models} ::: {#cell-setup-07 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} using TidierData using DataFrames, CSV using GLM, StatsModels, StatsBase, Statistics, Distributions using HypothesisTests using CairoMakie using MixedModels CairoMakie.activate!(type = "png") ponds = @chain CSV.read(joinpath("..", "data", "ponds.csv"), DataFrame) begin @drop_missing(canopy) @mutate(log_area = log(area_m2)) end nrow(ponds) ``` ::: {#setup-07 .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 173 ``` ::: ::: ## Hypothesis tests {#sec-tests} Before models, the basics. `HypothesisTests.jl` covers the usual repertoire. ::: {#cell-ttest .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} perm = @chain ponds begin @filter(hydro == "permanent") end temp_ = @chain ponds begin @filter(hydro == "temporary") end UnequalVarianceTTest(perm.richness, temp_.richness) ``` ::: {#ttest .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` Two sample t-test (unequal variance) ------------------------------------ Population details: parameter of interest: Mean difference value under h_0: 0 point estimate: 1.01849 95% confidence interval: (-0.452, 2.489) Test summary: outcome with 95% confidence: fail to reject h_0 two-sided p-value: 0.1734 Details: number of observations: [95,78] t-statistic: 1.3673234271337709 degrees of freedom: 168.03764735213443 empirical standard error: 0.7448775533304762 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.r-equivalent} **In R** `t.test(richness ~ hydro, data = ponds)` uses Welch by default — the same as `UnequalVarianceTTest`. For the equal-variance test, use `EqualVarianceTTest`. ::: ::: {#cell-other-tests .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} # normality and correlation ( ks_normal = ExactOneSampleKSTest( (ponds.body_size .- mean(ponds.body_size)) ./ std(ponds.body_size), Normal(0, 1)) |> pvalue, correlation = CorrelationTest(ponds.canopy, ponds.body_size) |> pvalue, ) ``` ::: {#other-tests .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (ks_normal = 0.9802464726099859, correlation = 4.331805547836094e-5) ``` ::: ::: ## Simple linear regression {#sec-simple-lm} The dataset's continuous response is `body_size`, mean body size. ::: {#cell-simple-lm .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} m1 = lm(@formula(body_size ~ temp_c), ponds) ``` ::: {#simple-lm .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` StatsModels.TableRegressionModel{LinearModel{GLM.LmResp{Vector{Float64}}, GLM.DensePredChol{Float64, LinearAlgebra.CholeskyPivoted{Float64, Matrix{Float64}, Vector{Int64}}}}, Matrix{Float64}} body_size ~ 1 + temp_c Coefficients: ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Coef. Std. Error t Pr(>|t|) Lower 95% Upper 95% ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── (Intercept) 13.1837 1.5861 8.31 <1e-13 10.0528 16.3145 temp_c 0.921736 0.0645072 14.29 <1e-30 0.794403 1.04907 ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── ``` ::: ::: The formula interface of `StatsModels.jl` matches R's: `~`, `+`, `*`, `:`, `-1` and inline transformations such as `log(x)` all work as expected. ::: {#cell-lm-extractors .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} ( r2 = r2(m1), adj_r2 = adjr2(m1), aic = aic(m1), coefs = coef(m1), intervals = confint(m1), ) ``` ::: {#lm-extractors .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (r2 = 0.544209635943369, adj_r2 = 0.5415441952178917, aic = 801.3969591368274, coefs = [13.18368268706997, 0.9217361109462694], intervals = [10.05281805410435 16.31454732003559; 0.7944032137607225 1.0490690081318161]) ``` ::: ::: ## Multiple regression {#sec-multiple-lm} ::: {#cell-multiple-lm .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} m2 = lm(@formula(body_size ~ temp_c + canopy), ponds) ``` ::: {#multiple-lm .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` StatsModels.TableRegressionModel{LinearModel{GLM.LmResp{Vector{Float64}}, GLM.DensePredChol{Float64, LinearAlgebra.CholeskyPivoted{Float64, Matrix{Float64}, Vector{Int64}}}}, Matrix{Float64}} body_size ~ 1 + temp_c + canopy Coefficients: ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Coef. Julia has no consolidated equivalent; the diagnostics above are assembled by hand. This is a genuine gap, and exactly the kind of thing a community package would fix well. ::: ## Mixed models {#sec-mixed-models} `MixedModels.jl` [@mixedmodelsjl] is maintained by Douglas Bates, first author of `lme4` [@bates2015lme4], and uses the same formula notation — including `(1 | group)`. On performance: comparisons between the two depend heavily on the model, the size of the data and the random-effects structure, and I know of no published benchmark I can cite here. If fitting time matters for your problem, measure it on your own case. ::: {#cell-lmm .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} mm1 = fit(MixedModel, @formula(body_size ~ temp_c + canopy + (1 | region)), ponds) ``` ::: {#lmm .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

Fit `body_size ~ canopy` separately for each region and compare the coefficients with those of a model with a `canopy * region` interaction. 2. Does `m4` have a significant interaction? Interpret the coefficient. 3. Compare `mm1` with a fixed-effects model for `region`. When is each preferable?
